List, show, read and cancel the batch jobs a project's agents asked for.

With jobs.scheduler in the config (or --jobs), the agent in a sandbox can ask for batch jobs with codeflower-job; the app submits each, and it runs in a sandbox of its own with the same image, folders and network. Jobs keep running when the sandbox stops (unless jobs.on_stop is cancel), and the next sandbox of the project follows them again. These commands work without one.

PROJECT is a project's name in the projects directory, or its folder.


## Usage

```sh
codeflower jobs
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config string` |  | config directory with config.yaml (or set $CODEFLOWER_CONFIG; default ~/.codeflower) |
| `--env-dir string` |  | folder of the projects' env folders, for projects whose settings do not name one (or env_dir in the config) |
| `--projects-dir string` |  | folder of the projects started with --project (or projects_dir in the config; default ~/codeflower/projects) |

## Commands

- [`codeflower jobs cancel`](/reference/cli/codeflower-jobs-cancel/): Cancel jobs of a project
- [`codeflower jobs list`](/reference/cli/codeflower-jobs-list/): List a project's jobs, asking the scheduler about those still active
- [`codeflower jobs log`](/reference/cli/codeflower-jobs-log/): Print a job's output
- [`codeflower jobs show`](/reference/cli/codeflower-jobs-show/): Show a job: what it runs, with what, and how it ended
